source: Quiz 5 - Sessions 1-6: Model Training, Alignment, and the Agent Harness
question: You compare cat in a sentence about a sunny windowsill with cat in a sentence about an angry trainer. What should you expect inside the model?

options.text: Each block must print a different replacement word for cat
options.feedback: Blocks transform numerical representations. They do not print intermediate replacement words as a required part of interpretation.

options.text: The same token can have different contextual representations
options.feedback: The initial token identity does not force one interpretation. Attention can bring different surrounding information into its representation.

options.text: The vocabulary must contain a separate ID for each sentence
options.feedback: The cat-star diagram describes changing representations of the same token. Contextual interpretation does not require a new vocabulary entry for every sentence.

options.text: The two sentences must update different permanent weight values
options.feedback: Processing different contexts changes current representations. Ordinary inference does not update permanent weights for each sentence.
